title: Variable-length routing and padding strategy — draft notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working/brainstorm doc for handling variable sequence lengths in the serving runtime. The focus is on tradeoffs between padding policies, bucketing granularity, and kernel selection strategies, plus how those choices interact with KV cache layout and the continuous-batching scheduler. Goal is a pragmatic hybrid design that reduces wasted compute and memory while preserving tail-latency SLOs for interactive workloads.

Context / constraints:
- Latency SLO: 99th percentile < 220ms for interactive tiers (token generation step), 50ms for fast-path routes.
- Typical request length distribution (observed, prod alpha): median 18 tokens, 75th 48, 90th 190, 99th 760.
- Hardware: mixed GPU fleet (A100 40GB, H100 80GB) with quantized kernels available (q4, q8, int8) for many models.
- KV cache: per-request prefix KV. Size and alignment matter: large padding wastes both GPU memory and KB-sized KV allocations on chips with slot alignment constraints.
- Scheduler supports continuous batching with max-latency windows and a hot-path fast lane.

Definitions (for this doc):
- sequence_len = user-provided tokens + current generation length
- pad_to = policy rounding target used when materializing input tensors for kernel invocation
- bucket = collection of requests with the same pad_to which can be fused/packed
- kernel family = a kernel binary configured for (pad_alignment, dtype, optimizations) e.g., q4_pad32_optimized_attn

High-level options considered:
1) Pad-to-max-per-batch: simplest; pad all requests in batch to the largest length in batch. Pros: minimal internal fragmentation; cons: worst-case heavy for long outliers, scheduling complexity grows with variance.
2) Global fixed pad grid (e.g., powers-of-two or multiples of 16/32): every request is rounded up to a small set of canonical lengths. Pros: easy kernel specialization, small set of kernels; cons: quantization lines (requests of 65->128 wastes), can overpad many med-length requests.
3) Elastic bucketing (micro-buckets): create many small buckets (e.g., boundaries at 8,16,24,32,40,48,64,96,128,192,256,512,1024) and route requests to nearest bucket. Pros: lower average waste; cons: more kernels, maintenance overhead.
4) Hybrid fast-path + coarse backup: requests under X tokens go through a low-pad fast path (pad to 32/64) optimized for latency; longer requests route to batch worker that can accept higher padding.

Key interactions to reason about:
- Kernel proliferation vs. cold cache: more buckets -> more specialized kernels -> better peak throughput for that length but higher cold-start and code-cache pressure on GPUs.
- KV cache fragmentation: if bucket padding causes KV per-request memory to jump (pad-to-256 vs pad-to-64) we will reduce effective capacity on-device and increase eviction churn.
- Scheduler windows: binned batching may increase head-of-line blocking when waiting for enough same-bucket requests; continuous batching mitigates this but can interact poorly with strict SLOs.

Empirical microbench notes (summary of experiments run in perf-lab, Oct-Nov 2025):
- Setup: Llama-ish 13B, h100, autotuned kernels. Synthetic arrival trace matching prod quantiles.
- Pad-to-batch-max: throughput baseline 1.0x, 50th latency 85ms, 99th latency 340ms. Large variance due to occasional 1k token requests.
- Power-of-two grid (pad to 32/64/128/256/512/1024): x1.15 throughput, 99th 210ms but memory pressure high on 40GB GPUs; several OOMs when combined with KV cache hot sets.
- Micro-buckets with cutoffs at [8,16,32,48,64,96,128,192,256,512,1024]: x1.34 throughput, 99th 190ms. Kernel code-cache used ~30 distinct kernels; acceptable on h100 but problematic on older nodes.
- Hybrid fast-path (pad-to-32 for <=48 tokens) + micro-buckets for rest: x1.40 throughput, 50th 60ms, 99th 170ms, KV memory footprint down 18% vs micro-buckets alone.

Design proposal (recommended): hybrid approach with three coordinated layers:
A) Client/request classification & routing:
  - At admission time, compute request.requested_max_seq = user_len + (expected_max_generation || default 128). Use request-level hint if provided (client hints are optional).
  - If requested_max_seq <= 48: route to fast-path pool (pad_to=32). This is the low-latency lane.
  - Else if requested_max_seq <= 256: place into elastic bucket with fine boundaries (every 16 tokens up to 256).
  - Else: route to large-seq workers and pad to nearest 64 multiple (to reduce kernel explosion).

B) Bucketing & padding policy:
  - Buckets defined by breakpoints: [8,16,32,48,64,80,96,112,128,160,192,224,256,320,384,512,768,1024]. This gives good tradeoff between kernel count and waste.
  - pad_to = min(bucket_upper, pad_alignment(bucket_upper)) where pad_alignment(n) picks 8 or 16 based on hardware/quant dtype. For tiny GPUs choose 8, for H100 choose 16/32.
  - For fast-path <=48 pad_to=32 absolute; special fused kernel (fast_attn_small) is kept hot.

C) Kernel selection & management:
  - For each bucket we maintain a prioritized kernel list (family): [quant_q4_specialized, q8_general, fp16_general]. At runtime pick highest-priority kernel available on node that supports pad_alignment.
  - Lazy population: kernels are loaded on-demand; eviction policy favors keeping fast-path and top-3 high-traffic buckets resident.
  - Code-cache telemetry: track per-node kernel load/unload counts; if > threshold within interval, consider merging adjacent buckets to reduce churn.

D) KV cache alignment and memory plan:
  - KV storage units should be sized to the bucket pad_to not the raw request length to avoid reallocation during batched execution.
  - Two-tier KV cache: on-GPU hot-kv (for recent prefixes) and host-resident cold-kv (for large historical prefixes or rarely-used clients). Hot-kv entries are charged using pad_to footprint to estimate actual GPU RAM usage.
  - When a request is promoted to a larger bucket (e.g., due to generation exceeding hint), we avoid forcing immediate reallocation by using a small dynamic delta allocation and deferred compaction step at generation end. This prevents spikes.

E) Scheduler changes:
  - Continuous batching remains default. Introduce 'bucket-aware preemption' where fast-path buckets have shorter batching windows and higher priority. Large-bucket collectors can be preempted to preserve SLO for fast-path.
  - Implement adaptive wait-time threshold per bucket: wait_time(bucket) = min(global_max_wait, base_wait * sqrt(bucket_size_factor)). This reduces head-of-line for small buckets and increases packability for large buckets.

Instrumentation & metrics to add:
- Per-request: assigned_bucket, pad_to, kernel_used, kernel_load_time, kv_alloc_bytes, generation_hints_used.
- Node-level: resident_kernel_count, kernel_load_evictions, gpu_kv_hot_used_bytes, bucket_wait_histograms.
- Alert rules: kernel_eviction_rate > X over 5m, hot-kv usage > 85% capacity, fast-path 99th latency > 250ms.

Implementation notes / API changes:
- Extend request proto with optional uint32 expected_max_generation_hint. Document as "best-effort" and default to 128 if unset.
- New runtime config section: pad_grid (list of ints), fast_path_threshold, kernel_family_priorities, kv_hot_size_bytes, per-node_pad_alignment.
- Worker bootstrap will check hardware and set pad_alignment heuristics (cfg override allowed).

Tradeoffs and open risks:
- Kernel proliferation: micro-buckets increase number of binaries. We mitigate by merging low-traffic adjacent buckets and by prioritizing kernel families. Risk remains on heterogenous cluster sizes.
- Wrong client hints: overestimating expected_generation can push requests into larger buckets unnecessarily. We will monitor hint adoption and instrument usage; consider "hint_penalty" in routing logic.
- KV fragmentation: deferred compaction reduces spikes but temporarily increases fragmentation. Need eviction policies that consider fragmentation cost.

Open questions / action items (owners noted):
- Q1: What default pad_alignment should we pick per GPU family? (owner: Priya) -> PERF-PRF experiment to test pad alignments 8/16/32 across fleet. (LINK: JIRA-RT-1193).
- Q2: How aggressive should kernel eviction be? (owner: Liam) -> simulate with 30-day traffic trace; measure kernel churn vs memory pressure.
- Q3: How to encode hint semantics in public API without encouraging over-optimistic hints? (owner: Maya) -> doc consumer guidance + metric to penalize mishinting.
- Q4: Should we expose pad_to choice to customers for advanced routing? (owner: Product) -> product consult.

Short term roadmap (next 8 weeks):
- Week 1-2: implement request hint field + routing stub. Add metrics scaffold (owner: Maya, Evan).
- Week 3-4: implement bucket assignment logic and fast-path pool. Unit tests for pad_to correctness. (owner: Priya).
- Week 5-6: kernel-family priority config and kernel lazy-load + telemetry. Start lab perf runs. (owner: Liam).
- Week 7-8: integrate KV hot/cold manager adjustments, run end-to-end experiments, and prepare canary rollout on h100 pool. (owner: Maya).

Appendix: rough pseudocode for routing decision:

function assign_bucket(request):
  expected = request.hint_or_default(128) + request.user_tokens
  if expected <= 48: return {pool: 'fast-path', pad_to: 32}
  for b in pad_grid_sorted:
    if expected <= b: return {pool: 'standard', pad_to: align(b)}
  return {pool: 'large', pad_to: align(next_multiple_of_64(expected))}

Notes: align(n) consults node.pad_alignment policy and returns the smallest multiple >= n.

Meeting notes & unresolved items:
- 2026-01-19 design sync: consensus around hybrid approach; strong preference to keep explicit fast-path for <48 token requests.
- Need follow-up on cost model: compute wasted FLOPs due to padding vs operational cost of more frequent kernel loads. (action: Evan).

Related artifacts & references:
- perf lab traces: s3://perf-lab/variable-length-tests/oct2025
- design draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- linear task: LINEAR-2301 (pad-grid experimentation)
- jira: JIRA-RT-1193 (kv alignment investigation)

Status / notes: draft. This doc intentionally mixes strategy with tactical implementation details — convert to a formal spec once perf experiments validate the default pad_grid.
